title: Marras 2001: csa fibre corrected of rectus abdominis at L4 (M, supine)

imaging.modality: MRI 1.5 T Philips GyroScan, T1 spin echo
imaging.plane: transverse slices perpendicular to the scan table through approximate vertebral body centres T8-S1; areas then fibre-angle corrected (dot product with literature fibre directions)

quantity.name: csa_fibre_corrected
quantity.definition: anatomical CSA multiplied by cosine of fibre angle to the plane normal (authors may call it PCSA/physiological area; NOT volume/fibre-length PCSA); fibre angles from Dumas et al. [15]

source.authors: Marras WS, Jorgensen MJ, Granata KP, Wiand B
source.sample: young healthy volunteers (same 30 subjects/MRI scans as Jorgensen 2001)

protocol.summary: Supine MRI axial slices through vertebral body centres T8-S1; raw muscle areas corrected by the dot product with literature fibre-direction unit vectors (authors call the result ACSA).
how_to_simulate: Pose the model supine; cut a transverse plane perpendicular to the body long axis through the centre of the L4 vertebral body.
Select the model rect. abd fascicles crossing that plane on each side; sum their PCSA (fibre-angle-corrected area = area normal to the fibres).

Compare each side with the measured mean +/- SD (the measured value is the axial MRI area times the cosine of a literature fibre angle, so it approximates the summed PCSA of fibres crossing the slice, not the whole-muscle PCSA).

subject_model.source: Table 1 (vertebral body ACSA by level in Table 2, e.g. L3 14.13 cm2)

protocol.notes: Authors label Table 2 "fiber angle corrected ACSAs". Converted cm2 -> mm2 (x100). Uncorrected areas are not reported.

extraction.check_notes: Every cell compared with rendered (rotated) page 41; level columns confirmed from the image.
